Animal and veterinary sciences play a vital role in the management and care of livestock,

companion animals as well as those animals maintained at zoos, aquariums and laboratory animal facilities.
Options are available to students interested in animal sciences or veterinary medicine.
Graduates of this program will be prepared to use professional concentration courses: AVs 101, 102, 110, 304, 331, 332, 333, 343, 472 plus additional option-specific courses as indicated below.
Including the core courses, across options, there are 30-33 credits of professional concentration; 9 credits of basic non-science (C0M 100; WRT 104 or 106 and w RT 300+); 18-50 credits of basic science including Bl0 101/103 and Bl0 102/104; and 9-36 credits of supporting electives required for this major.

Animal Science Option.
This option includes lecture and lab-based coursework in animal management, nutrition, physiology. behavior, and disease, and provides broad flexibility for students in their choice of animal science courses.

Students have the option to focus their coursework specifically on domestic livestock, exotic animals or animal technology, or be more broadly focused.
Research techniques and procedures for animal care are emphasized along with a strong background in the local government agencies focused on animal care, welfare, and regulation.
Many work directly with animals as veterinary as high school agricultural teachers, conduct animal-based research in academic settings and private industry, or help bridge the gap between research and practical application as extension agents.
The option also provides strong entrepreneurial opportunities for graduates interested in establishing their own businesses, whether in food animal production, pet care and domestic or wildlife species.
In addition to the core courses specifed of the major, the following professional courses are required: AVS 212-or412; one 300+ (3 cr) animal management course; one 400-level animal science elective, one 300+ additional concentration course.

Students in this option will also be well prepared to pursue graduate programs in animal physiology. nutrition and health.
